feature: F4 — Wallet & Onboarding, plus the Operator Surface (/ops)
summary: Two surfaces that both exist to keep a promise the product makes elsewhere. Part A is the wallet layer: reading Insidor is free and complete, and a wallet is demanded only at the exact instant an action needs one, with the user's work (amount, ticker draft, coin identity) never discarded by the gate — including the funding cliff, where a user with a wallet and no SOL is the single highest-drop moment in the product. Part B is the operator surface: a health model of ten SLIs, each a named query, where SLI-2 (`stage_output_stall`) and SLI-4 (`board_render_fallback`) would have caught the two-day silent outage in ~10 minutes and at T+0 of user impact respectively, plus the user-facing honesty band that shows a stale board as stale and suppresses every earliness claim while the pipeline is dead.

screens.name: A1 · Board, signed out (first run)
screens.job: Prove the product works before asking for anything. Everything readable is readable; the wallet is demanded only at the instant of an action, in place, without discarding the user's work.
screens.layout: Identical to the connected board — no reduced/teaser variant exists. Existing `.shell` grid `1fr 460px`, `.main` padding 26px 26px 80px, narrative table capped 980px, token tables 1140px, `.rail` 460px sticky. Nav is `.nav` 58px with `.brand`, `.navlinks` (Trending/Search/You), `.navsearch` (⌘K), `.solpill`, `#userAuth`. No blur, no overlay, no lock icons, no row-count cap, no 'sign up to see more'.

screens.name: B1 · /ops — pipeline health
screens.job: Tell one person in under three seconds whether the product's core claim is true right now, and if not, which of eleven stages broke.
screens.layout: Same shell as the app (`1fr 460px`), main capped 1140px, so the operator is not learning a second layout under stress. Six stacked regions, all `.ttable` skin, 14px gaps. Server-gated: route handler checks the Privy DID against `OPS_ALLOWLIST` server-side and 404s otherwise — never a client-side check. THE OPERATOR LOOKS AT REGION 0, THEN REGION 2. Region 0 is the verdict; region 2 is the funnel, and every real outage of this pipeline appears as a column of zeros in the funnel, which names the broken stage without reading a log.

elements.shows: Grid `auto 1fr auto`. Left: 14px dot, lime/amber/red, `animation:pulse 2s` only when healthy. Centre: `.ops-state` Clash Display 34px uppercase — `HEALTHY` / `DEGRADED` / `DEAD` — and under it `.ops-why` mono 12.5px muted naming the single worst breaching SLI: `worst: stage_output_stall = 7 consecutive zero runs · ingest · since 14:02 UTC (2h 11m)`. Right: `.ops-clock` mono 11px dim: `evaluated 18s ago · watchdog ok · healthchecks ok 41s ago`.
elements.source: `ops_sli_sample` latest row per SLI, ranked by severity then breach duration
elements.interaction: Click the `.ops-why` → scrolls and highlights that SLI's row in region 1.

elements.shows: Header `# | SLI | Value | Warn | Page | State | Breaching for | Last 60m`. Grid `26px minmax(170px,1.4fr) .85fr .55fr .55fr 96px .85fr 112px`, gap 12, padding 13px 20px, min-height 50px. SLI name in `var(--mono)` 12px ink. Value mono 13px right-aligned, coloured by state. State cell reuses `.timing-pill`: `.timing-early` (lime) = ok, `.timing-mid` (amber) = warn, `.timing-late` (red) = page. Sparkline reuses `.spark` SVG, viewBox `0 0 100 24`, ion stroke, red fill band above the page threshold.
elements.source: `ops_sli_sample` (NEW) — one row per SLI per 60s. Ten SLIs and their exact queries are in `mechanism`.
elements.interaction: Row click expands an inline `.mini` block with the raw query text and a `copy` control, so the operator can run it against Supabase directly.

elements.shows: Six equal `.qs`-skin cells with `::before` hairline dividers, separated by `→` glyphs carrying the conversion rate in mono 10px dim. Per cell: `.k` uppercase 9.5px dim label (ARRIVED / ADMITTED / TRACKED / TRIGGERED / CLUSTERED / PROMOTED), `.v` mono 22px value for the last 60 min, a `.chgpill` up/down vs the 7-day same-hour baseline, and a 22px `.spark` over 6h. A zero renders at 22px in `var(--red)` with a `0` — never dim, never `—`. Conversions read `31%` `→` `88%` `→` `22%` `→` `41%` `→` `6%`.
elements.source: `ops_funnel` (NEW) — persists what `worker/lib/funnel-log.js` currently only writes to stdout. THIS IS THE CENTRAL GAP: the funnel data exists in-process today and is thrown away.
elements.interaction: Cell click → filters region 3 to the stage that owns it.

elements.shows: `Stage | Last success | Last attempt | p50 dur | Errors 1h | Rows out | Last error`. Rows: `ingest-x`, `ingest-tt`, `snapshot`, `score`, `cluster`, `resolve-coins`, `trends`. The `Last error` cell renders `402 payment_required · twitterapi.io · 14:02:11` in mono 11px `var(--red)`. THIS IS THE CELL THAT WAS INVISIBLE FOR TWO DAYS — the retry helper only retried 429, so a 402 threw, was never recorded, and vanished.
elements.source: `ops_stage_run` (NEW): `{stage, started_at, finished_at, ok, rows_in, rows_out, error_class, http_status, message}`
elements.interaction: Click a stage → rail switches to `Errors` filtered to it.

Projected EOD = `cost_usd / day_fraction_elapsed`, mono, red when it exceeds the cap.

Cycles: `worker`, `ingested/pruned/snapshots`, `ran_at`.

states: healthy — verdict lime, all 10 SLIs `.timing-early`
degraded — verdict amber; at least one warn, no page-level breach; board is still truthful
dead — verdict red; any of SLI 1/2/3/4 breaching at page level

evaluator stale — if the newest `ops_sli_sample` is >3 min old the verdict strip greys out entirely and reads `UNKNOWN · the evaluator itself has not reported since 14:41`. A green board from a dead evaluator is the failure mode that caused the outage; never render one.
cold start / no baseline — funnel `.chgpill`s render `—` rather than a delta against fewer than 3 days of history
budget-starved — region 4 red, verdict DEGRADED with `.ops-why` = `budget_burn twitterapi.io 1.00 before 12:00 UTC`
scoring paused — the existing `.scoring-paused-banner` (amber, `Meme scoring paused / Anthropic budget exhausted`) is hoisted from the app rail to the top of region 0
unauthorised — server 404, no login prompt, no hint the route exists

mechanism:
## PART A — MECHANISM

### A.1 The gate predicate — one function, three tiers
```ts
// features/wallet/model/gate.ts  (PURE — mandatory tests)
type Gate = 'open' | 'needs-wallet' | 'needs-sol';
function gateFor(action: Action, w: WalletState): Gate {
  if (action.kind === 'read' || action.kind === 'follow') return 'open';   // follow persists locally
  if (!w.connected) return 'needs-wallet';
  if (action.kind === 'comment') return 'open';                            // no SOL required to post
  const need = action.solIn + GAS_RESERVE_SOL;                             // 0.02
  return (w.solBalance ?? 0) >= need ? 'open' : 'needs-sol';
}
```
Reads, follows and comments never touch the funding path. Only `buy` and `create` can return `needs-sol`. `create` costs `0.02 (rent+fee) + firstBuy` — the existing `~1.02 SOL` figure is `0.52 + firstBuy` and must be replaced with a real quoted fee.

### A.2 Privy configuration — v3 facts that will otherwise break the build
```ts
<PrivyProvider appId={APP_ID} config={{
  appearance: { theme:'dark', accentColor:'#3DE0FF',
                walletChainType:'solana-only',       // REQUIRED — v3 default is 'ethereum-only'
                showWalletLoginFirst:true,
                walletList:['phantom','solflare','backpack','detected_solana_wallets'] },
  loginMethods:['wallet','email','google'],
  embeddedWallets:{ createOnLogin:'users-without-wallets' },
  externalWallets:{ solana:{ connectors: toSolanaWalletConnectors({shouldAutoConnect:false}) } },
}}>
```
- `useSolanaWallets` **does not exist in v3** (zero hits across all `.d.ts`; Privy's own docs still reference it). Use `useWallets()` / `useCreateWallet()` / `useExportWallet()` from `@privy-io/react-auth/solana`.
- The package ships **no `use client` banner** — put it on our own provider wrapper, mount near root, gate every consumer on `usePrivy().ready`.
- Four Solana peer deps are `optional:true` and will resolve differently in clean CI: declare `@solana/kit`, `@solana-program/system`, `@solana-program/token`, `@solana-program/memo` explicitly.
- Signing is raw bytes: `useSignTransaction()` → `{transaction: Uint8Array}` → `{signedTransaction: Uint8Array}`. Base64↔Uint8Array is the only conversion needed for Jupiter `/swap/v2/execute`; do **not** pull in `@solana/web3.js` v1 or a `WalletContextState` shim.
- **Token refresh loop is mandatory.** Privy access tokens live ~1h; Supabase Realtime caches channel auth for the connection lifetime and disconnects on JWT expiry. Without `getAccessToken()` on a 50-minute timer feeding `supabase.realtime.setAuth()`, every user silently drops off the live feed after an hour. This is the most likely launch-day bug in the design.

### A.3 Funding-cliff arithmetic — the number shown to the user
```
target_sol   = amount_in + 0.02                                  // gas reserve, never spendable
deficit_sol  = max(0, target_sol - balance_sol)

CARD PATH (two legs, and we say so):
  leg1 fiat→SOL:  gross_usd
                  − provider_fee (2.5%–4.9%, READ FROM THE QUOTE, never hardcoded)
                  − network      (~0.000005 SOL)
                  = sol_received
  leg2 SOL→mint:  Jupiter /swap/v2/order
                  − route/LP fee (from quote.routePlan)
                  − Insidor referralFee (50 bps; Jupiter keeps 20% of it)
                  − priceImpactPct
                  − priority fee (0.0005 fast / 0.002 turbo SOL)
                  = tokens_out
  displayed: "$50 in → about $45.90 of $HORN out."   (one number, both legs)

SEND PATH:  0 fee, ~30s, only leg2 costs apply.
SWAP PATH:  USDC→SOL via Jupiter, then leg2.
```
If the provider quote fails, the card tile disables with a reason. A guessed percentage on a screen about money is worse than an absent one.

**Resume**: `localStorage['insidor.trade-intent.v1']` + a `getBalance` poll every 6s (max 150 polls / 15 min / 150 Helius credits). On satisfaction the trade panel is restored with the amount pre-filled — the user never re-navigates to the coin.

### A.4 Position badge derivation (server-side, at write time only)
```
POST /api/comment
  1. verify Privy token with @privy-io/node@0.27.0  → privy_did → app_user
  2. moderation pre-pass (address gate first: any base58 32–44 char that is NOT
     one of this narrative's mints → block, no appeal — ~90% of spam, one lookup)
  3. mint = top CONFIRMED coin of the story, else null
  4. if mint:
       helius getTokenAccountsByOwner(author_wallet, {mint}, {encoding:'jsonParsed'})  // 1 credit
       ui = Σ tokenAmount.uiAmount
       prior = max(snap_position_lamports) for (author_wallet, mint) in comment
       state = ui > 0 ? 'holds' : (prior > 0 ? 'sold' : 'none')
     on RPC error/timeout → state = 'unknown'      // NEVER 'none'
  5. insert comment with snap_views, snap_coin_count, snap_age_min, snap_top_mcap,
     snap_position_lamports, snap_position_mint, snap_position_state
```
The snapshot is immutable. Rendering it live would rewrite history and destroy the only non-gameable ranking signal the product has.

## PART B — MECHANISM

### B.1 The health model: healthy ⇔ all ten SLIs non-breaching
A heartbeat proves a process **ran**, not that it **produced anything** — `worker_pipeline_state.last_heartbeat` would have ticked happily through all 48 hours. Every SLI below is therefore an **output** measure, and the evaluator lives where the pipeline's death cannot silence it.

| # | SLI | Warn | **Page** | Class | Caught the outage? |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `ingest_freshness` | 15 m | **30 m** | dead | ✅ |
| 2 | `stage_output_stall` | 3 runs | **5 runs (~10 m)** | dead | ✅ **fastest** |
| 3 | `gate_supply` | <8 | **0 for 10 m** | dead | ✅ |
| 4 | `board_render_fallback` | — | **≥1, immediately** | dead | ✅ **at T+0 of user impact** |
| 5 | `stage_liveness` | 2× interval | **3×** | degraded | crash-loop |
| 6 | `funnel_yield` | −2σ | **−3σ** | degraded | "runs but the floor is too high" |
| 7 | `budget_burn` | 0.90 | **1.0 before 12:00 UTC** | degraded | budget starvation |
| 8 | `tick_freshness` | 60 s | **120 s** | dead | board froze |
| 9 | `lead_time_p50` | <15 m | **<8 m** | degraded | the claim is failing |
| 10 | `delta_divergence` | 1% | **5%** | degraded | reconciliation bug |

**SLI-2 is the one that would have caught the two-day outage within minutes**, and it costs nothing — `worker_cycle_log` already records `ingested` per run.

### B.2 The queries, verbatim

**SLI-1 `ingest_freshness`**
```sql
select extract(epoch from (now() - max(first_seen_at)))/60 as ingest_freshness_min,
       count(*) filter (where first_seen_at > now() - interval '15 minutes') as posts_15m
from narrative_posts;
```

**SLI-2 `stage_output_stall` — the one that catches a silent death**
```sql
with runs as (
  select worker, ran_at, coalesce(ingested,0) as out_rows,
         row_number() over (partition by worker order by ran_at desc) as rn
  from worker_cycle_log
  where ran_at > now() - interval '6 hours'
)
select worker,
       coalesce(min(rn) filter (where out_rows > 0) - 1, 999) as zero_run_streak,
       max(ran_at) as last_run
from runs group by worker;
```
`999` (never produced anything in 6h) pages immediately.

**SLI-3 `gate_supply`**
```sql
select count(*) as eligible,
       count(*) filter (where updated_at > now() - interval '30 minutes') as eligible_fresh
from narratives where display_eligible = true;
```

**SLI-4 `board_render_fallback` — sharpest, near-zero cost**
```sql
select count(*) as fallback_renders_5m
from ops_event where kind = 'board_fallback' and ts > now() - interval '5 minutes';
```
Emitter: `lib/stories.ts` **already computes `showingIneligible` and returns it in silence.** One fire-and-forget insert (deduped 60 s per instance) turns the code's own knowledge that the board is broken into a page.

**SLI-5 `stage_liveness`**
```sql
select s.stage,
       extract(epoch from (now() - s.last_run))/60 as minutes_since,
       s.interval_min
from worker_pipeline_state w,
lateral (values
  ('ingest',   w.last_run_ingest,   5),
  ('snapshot', w.last_run_snapshot, 5),
  ('score',    w.last_run_score,    5),
  ('cluster',  w.last_run_cluster,  2),
  ('trends',   w.last_run_trends,  60)
) as s(stage, last_run, interval_min)
where w.id = 1;
```

**SLI-6 `funnel_yield`**
```sql
with cur as (
  select sum(arrived)::numeric a, sum(admitted)::numeric b
  from ops_funnel where ts > now() - interval '60 minutes'
), base as (
  select avg(r) mu, stddev_samp(r) sd from (
    select sum(admitted)::numeric / nullif(sum(arrived),0) r
    from ops_funnel
    where ts between now() - interval '7 days' and now() - interval '1 hour'
    group by date_trunc('hour', ts)
  ) h
)
select (select b/nullif(a,0) from cur) as yield_now, mu, sd,
       ((select b/nullif(a,0) from cur) - mu) / nullif(sd,0) as z
from base;
```

**SLI-7 `budget_burn`**
```sql
select u.source, u.reads_today, u.cost_usd, c.daily_cap_usd,
       u.cost_usd / nullif(c.daily_cap_usd,0) as burn_frac,
       (extract(epoch from (now() at time zone 'utc') - date_trunc('day', now() at time zone 'utc')) / 86400.0) as day_frac,
       u.cost_usd / nullif(extract(epoch from (now() at time zone 'utc') - date_trunc('day', now() at time zone 'utc'))/86400.0, 0) as projected_eod
from worker_usage u
join ops_budget_cap c on c.source = u.source
where u.utc_date = (current_date at time zone 'utc');
```

**SLI-8 `tick_freshness`**
```sql
select extract(epoch from (now() - max(updated_at))) as seconds_since_tick
from narratives where display_eligible = true;
```

**SLI-9 `lead_time_p50` (also the ledger query for B2)**
```sql
select percentile_cont(0.50) within group (order by lead_min) as p50,
       percentile_cont(0.25) within group (order by lead_min) as p25,
       percentile_cont(0.75) within group (order by lead_min) as p75,
       count(*) as n,
       count(*) filter (where lead_min < 0)::numeric / nullif(count(*),0) as late_rate
from (
  select n.id, n.title, n.promoted_at, m.first_mint_at, c.first_ct_at,
         extract(epoch from (least(m.first_mint_at, c.first_ct_at) - n.promoted_at))/60 as lead_min
  from narratives n
  left join lateral (
    select min(cm.mint_time) as first_mint_at
    from narrative_tickers nt join coin_mints cm on cm.mint = nt.mint_ca
    where nt.narrative_id = n.id and nt.match_state = 'CONFIRMED'
  ) m on true
  left join lateral (
    select min(x.posted_at) as first_ct_at from ct_mentions x where x.narrative_id = n.id
  ) c on true
  where n.promoted_at > now() - interval '7 days'
    and n.earliness_eligible = true
    and least(m.first_mint_at, c.first_ct_at) is not null
    and least(m.first_mint_at, c.first_ct_at) < n.promoted_at + interval '6 hours'
    and not exists (                                  -- exclude mint-clock blind spots
      select 1 from ops_event g
      where g.kind = 'mint_stream_gap'
        and tstzrange((g.detail->>'from')::timestamptz, (g.detail->>'to')::timestamptz)
            @> n.promoted_at)
) t;
```

**SLI-10 `delta_divergence`**
```sql
select count(*) filter (where kind='client_resync')::numeric
     / nullif(count(*) filter (where kind='client_session'),0) as resync_rate
from ops_event where ts > now() - interval '15 minutes';
```

**Funnel (region 2) and gate mix (region 5)**
```sql
select date_trunc('minute', ts) t, sum(arrived) arrived, sum(admitted) admitted,
       sum(tracked) tracked, sum(triggered) triggered, sum(clustered) clustered,
       sum(promoted) promoted
from ops_funnel where ts > now() - interval '6 hours' group by 1 order by 1;

-- 5-minute sampler feeding the gate chart
insert into ops_sli_sample(ts, sli, value)
select now(), 'gate_mix', jsonb_object_agg(coalesce(gate_reason,'unknown'), c)
from (select gate_reason, count(*) c from narratives
      where updated_at > now() - interval '24 hours' group by 1) x;
```
`gate_reason` values are already emitted by `worker/lib/cluster-engine.js:deriveGateReason`: `too_old`, `below_views`, `low_meme`, `no_replication`, `no_velocity`, `eligible`.

### B.3 Alerts — degraded vs dead

**DEAD** = the product's core claim is false right now. SLIs 1, 2, 3, 4, 8.
→ Slack `#insidor-alerts` with `@channel`, red attachment, the offending SLI's value, the query, and a one-click `/ops` deep link. **Repeats every 15 min until acked** with `/ack <sli>`. Ack expires after 2 h and the alert re-fires.

**DEGRADED** = quality reduced, board still truthful. SLIs 5, 6, 7, 9, 10.
→ Slack `#insidor-ops`, amber, **one message, threaded, auto-resolves**, never repeats, never a phone.

**Three independent observers, because any one of them can be the thing that died:**
1. **Watchdog** — Inngest function, cron every 2 min, `concurrency:{limit:1}`. Evaluates all ten, writes `ops_sli_sample`, posts to Slack, then pings healthchecks.io.
2. **External dead-man** — healthchecks.io expects that ping every 2 min with a 5 min grace. If Inngest, Vercel or the watchdog itself dies, healthchecks emails+SMSes at T+5. **Nothing inside the system can suppress this.**
3. **In-database** — `pg_cron` every 5 min → `evaluate_health()` → `pg_net` POST to the Slack webhook on any page-level breach. Survives total loss of the app platform.

**Replay against the real incident:** T+4 min warn on SLI-2, **T+10 min page** on SLI-2, T+30 min page on SLI-1, and an immediate page the instant the first user hits `showingIneligible`. Detection ~10 minutes. Was: 2 days.

### B.4 The bug that made it silent, and the fix
`worker/lib/retry.js` defaults to `retryOn: err => err.status === 429`. A 402 from twitterapi.io (out of credit) is not retryable, so it **threw** — and because no stage wraps its own failure in a recorded row, the throw vanished into a log nobody reads.
```js
const RETRYABLE  = new Set([408, 425, 429, 500, 502, 503, 504]);
const FATAL_LOUD = new Set([401, 402, 403, 429_permanent]);  // credential / billing
retryOn: err => RETRYABLE.has(err.status)
```
Plus a mandatory `worker/lib/stage-run.js` wrapper:
```js
await recordStage(sb, 'ingest-x', async () => { ... });
// writes ops_stage_run { stage, started_at, finished_at, ok,
//   rows_in, rows_out, http_status, error_class, message }
```
`error_class ∈ {payment_required, unauthorized, rate_limited, upstream_5xx, timeout, parse, unknown}`. Any `payment_required` or `unauthorized` row pages immediately regardless of the SLI table — a billing failure is not a statistical condition to be averaged.

### B.5 The degrade tiers as one computed value
```ts
// features/ops/model/freshness.ts  (PURE)
type Tier = 'fresh' | 'lagging' | 'stale' | 'fallback';
function tier(h: PipelineHealth): Tier {
  if (h.showingIneligible) return 'fallback';
  if (h.eligibleCount === 0) return 'stale';
  if (h.minutesStale == null) return 'stale';       // unknown fails to stale, not to fresh
  if (h.minutesStale > 45) return 'stale';
  if (h.minutesStale > 15) return 'lagging';
  return 'fresh';
}
const showLeadClaims = (t: Tier) => t === 'fresh' || t === 'lagging';
```
`showLeadClaims` is the load-bearing line: under `stale`/`fallback` every `+31m early` badge is removed from every surface. A dimmed earliness badge on a dead pipeline is still an earliness claim.

Blocks the localStorage→account merge in A1. | | `holding(user_id, mint, narrative_id, tokens, cost_sol, entry_price, opened_at, minutes_early)` | `minutes_early` is the number the product is about, and it must be allowed to be **negative and shown**. | | `comment(id, narrative_id, user_id, author_wallet, body, status, created_at, snap_views, snap_coin_count, snap_age_min, snap_top_mcap, snap_position_lamports, snap_position_mint, snap_position_state)` | The stamp is **unrecoverable retroactively** — build it before comments ship. `snap_position_state ∈ holds\|sold\|none\|unknown` is what makes A4's fail-closed rule expressible. | | `trade_intent(user_id, mint, side, amount_sol, slippage_bps, created_at, expires_at, state)` | Optional server mirror of the localStorage intent, so the funding cliff survives a device switch. | | `poster` / `payout` | Not needed for F4; named because the create path's fee split (`.split` panel) is static markup today claiming 3%/1%, while the flow doc specifies maker 50 / poster 40 / Insidor 10. **The UI currently asserts a number the system does not implement.** | ## 🔴 DOES NOT EXIST — PART B | Object | Why it blocks | |---|---| | `narratives.promoted_at timestamptz` | **The single most important missing column.** Lead time is measured from PROMOTE and `promoted_at` must be set once, forever. Today `lead_time_min` is assigned at gate time as `narr.lead_time_min ?? narr.age_min` and recomputed on every cluster cycle — so it is not a fixed clock and B2 cannot be built on it. | | `narratives.earliness_eligible boolean` | Left-censored entries (first seen already large) must be permanently excluded from the earliness denominator or the headline number is a lie. | | `narrative_tickers.source text ('cashtag'\|'llm'\|'mint_in_post')` | No provenance column exists, so an LLM-invented ticker is indistinguishable from a real cashtag downstream. Root cause of the $KANG class. | | `narrative_tickers.match_state ('CONFIRMED'\|'UNSURE'\|'REJECTED')`, `.match_score numeric`, `.mint_time timestamptz`, `.evidence jsonb` | **THE ONE RULE is uncomputable without `match_state`** — the primary button is a function of the CONFIRMED count and there is no CONFIRMED. Also gates B2's precision numerator and the abstain-band monitoring. | | `coin_mints(mint pk, mint_time, first_seen_at, symbol, name, creator, source)` | Clock A (PumpPortal `subscribeNewToken`). Without it `t_mint` does not exist and B2 cannot compute lead time at all. | | `ct_mentions(id, handle, platform_post_id, posted_at, text, narrative_id, first_seen_at)` | Clock B (~300 CT accounts @ 2 min). `t_crypto = min(t_mint, t_ct)`. Both indexes must be written **before** any alert or the number has lookahead bias. | | `ops_funnel(ts, stage, platform, arrived, admitted, tracked, triggered, clustered, promoted)` | **The funnel data is computed in-process today and thrown away** — `worker/lib/funnel-log.js` only `console.log`s it. Region 2 and SLI-6 are both blocked on persisting it. | | `ops_stage_run(id, stage, started_at, finished_at, ok, rows_in, rows_out, http_status, error_class, message)` | The 402 had nowhere to be recorded. This table is the fix. | | `ops_event(id, ts, kind, severity, subject, detail jsonb)` | Kinds: `board_fallback` (SLI-4), `alert_fired`, `alert_resolved`, `mint_stream_gap`, `wallet_export`, `client_resync`, `client_session`. | | `ops_sli_sample(ts, sli, value jsonb, state)` | Needed for "0 for 10 minutes" style thresholds, the 60m sparklines, and the region-5 gate chart. Without history every SLI is instantaneous and cannot express duration. | | `ops_budget_cap(source pk, daily_cap_usd, daily_cap_reads)` | Caps live in env/code today and are therefore not joinable in region 4. | | `evaluate_health()` pg function + `pg_cron` + `pg_net` | The in-database third observer. | ## OTHER FLAGGED GAPS (existing code, not schema) - `.pendbanner` **container has no CSS** (only its `b`) — B3's honesty band is spec'd into that slot and defines it. - `.solpill` markup **does not exist in any commit** although the CSS and `live.js:renderSolNav()` driver do — A1 requires it. - `.auth-panel` is fully styled and never rendered; A4's account panel ports it rather than inventing one. - `.dim` has **no CSS rule** despite being used in `#bal`, the safety-check unknown state, and the trade note — intended `color:var(--dim)` (`#5A5A62`). A4's `Balance —` state depends on it. - `updated now` writes the literal string `now` every 4 s — a fabricated freshness signal that must be deleted before B3 ships, or the honesty band contradicts the chrome above it. - `api/safety.js` reads authority fields off RugCheck `/report/summary`, which does not contain them, and emits `mintRevoked:true` for USDC. Not a wallet bug, but it is the same fail-open pattern as the position badge and should be fixed alongside it (`/v1/tokens/{mint}/report`). - `lib/token-lookup.js:70` `if (!pair.pairCreatedAt) return 0;` — missing timestamp renders as `ageMin = 0`, i.e. "brand new", on a terminal that sells earliness. Same class as `no position` on a failed read.
buildOrder: B0 · Two hours, zero new infra, closes the outage class: widen `worker/lib/retry.js` retryOn to {408,425,429,500,502,503,504}; add `worker/lib/stage-run.js` + `ops_stage_run` and wrap all seven stages; make `lib/stories.ts` emit `ops_event(kind='board_fallback')` on the `showingIneligible` it already computes. Ship alone — this is the incident fix.

B1 · The watchdog and the dead-man in one PR: `ops_sli_sample`, `ops_event`, `ops_budget_cap`; an Inngest `watchdog` cron @2min evaluating SLIs 1,2,3,4,5,7,8 (the seven that need no new clocks); Slack webhook with the degraded/dead split; healthchecks.io ping. SLI-2 alone retires the two-day failure mode. Do NOT ship the dashboard first — alerting without a dashboard is useful; a dashboard nobody is looking at is not.
B2 · Persist the funnel: `ops_funnel` table, `funnel-log.js` writes rows as well as stdout, `pg_cron` + `pg_net` `evaluate_health()` as the third observer. Unblocks SLI-6.
B3 · `/ops` regions 0–4 (verdict, SLI table, funnel, stages, spend) behind the server-side DID allowlist. Region 5 needs only the `gate_mix` sampler from B2.

A1 · Wallet provider + gate: `PrivyProvider` wrapper with `walletChainType:'solana-only'` and the 50-min `getAccessToken` → `realtime.setAuth()` refresh loop; `features/wallet/model/gate.ts` with tests; `app_user` + `follow` tables; `.gate-inline`; localStorage follow set with account merge. Board is unchanged and fully readable — this step adds no visible gate that was not already there.
A2 · Connect sheet (both paths) + `.user-chip` balance + ported `.account-panel` + the `.solpill` markup that has never existed. Trade panel gets real signed-out quotes and the intent handoff.

A3 · The funding cliff: `.fundbox` in-place panel, send/card/swap tiles, the two-leg cost line read from live quotes, `trade_intent` + the 6-second balance watcher and auto-resume. Highest-drop moment, so it ships as its own release with funnel instrumentation on every tile.
A4 · Export & security section in `/you`, `useExportWallet`, the 3-second dwell, the never-exported-with-balance nudge, `ops_event(kind='wallet_export')`.

B4 · The honesty band: `features/ops/model/freshness.ts` tier function with tests, the `.pendbanner` container style, the four tiers, and — the load-bearing part — `showLeadClaims` suppressing every `.lead-badge` under stale/fallback. Delete the `tokUpd` fake-freshness interval in the same PR.

B5 · The clocks: `coin_mints` from the PumpPortal singleton (supervised, heartbeat, gap-detection writing `ops_event(kind='mint_stream_gap')`), `ct_mentions` from the ~300-account poll, `narratives.promoted_at` set once at PROMOTE plus `earliness_eligible`. Nothing about lead time is measurable before this.
B6 · `/ops/earliness` ledger + SLI-9 + the public `/record` projection off the identical query, with the `All`-default filter asserted in a CI test.

A5 · Comment position stamp: `comment` table with all six snap columns, the server-side write path with the address gate and the fail-closed `unknown` state, `.pos-badge`. Ships with moderation in the same release, never before it.
openQuestions: Card-onramp fee is quoted as 2.5–4.9% but that spread is provider/region/amount dependent and both `useAddFunds` and `useFiatOnramp` are `@experimental`. Run a live $50 quote against a target mint before any copy claims a number — and decide the fallback if Privy's experimental hooks change shape mid-beta.

Does the funding cliff justify a sponsored first trade? Insidor could subsidise the ~$2 card fee on a user's first buy under $50 and recover it from Jupiter referral over subsequent trades. That is a founder call about CAC, not a design call, but it changes A3's layout (a fourth tile) materially.

Should `trade_intent` live server-side at all, or is localStorage sufficient? Server-side survives a device switch and gives a real drop-off funnel; it also means we store an unexecuted trading intention, which is a different data-retention posture.

Privy `role` claim: Supabase third-party auth needs `role:"authenticated"` in the JWT and Privy documents no claim-injection hook. We ship server-side writes via service role for now — but if the answer from Privy support is 'never', the comment write path stays a route handler permanently and RLS-on-the-client is off the table for good.
What is the ops allowlist mechanism at scale — env var of Privy DIDs is fine for 3 people and wrong at 15. Does `/ops` get a real role on `app_user`, and if so who grants it?

SLI-9's page threshold (`lead_time_p50 < 8m`) fires on a product-quality regression, not an outage. Paging on it at 3am is arguably wrong. Should it be a daily digest instead, with paging reserved for the five dead-class SLIs?

Abstain-rate monitoring: the design says 15–30% is healthy and a rising rate is a signal, not a failure. What is the actual alert shape — a warn at >35% sustained 6h, or a weekly review item? Alerting on it invites threshold-lowering, which defeats D1.

The `sold` position state needs either a prior snapshot for the same (wallet, mint) or a Helius `getTransactionsForAddress` call. The first is free but only works if the user commented before selling; the second costs credits on every comment. Which, and is `sold` worth the cost versus collapsing it into `no position`? (Recommendation: keep it — 'talking their book after exiting' is exactly what the badge exists to expose.)

Nothing in this spec covers what a user sees when their own launched coin's story is later reclassified NEVER-SURFACE under D3. The coin exists, the wallet holds fees, and the story is gone from every board. That state needs a decision before creation ships.

Status-page convention (GitHub, Cloudflare): name the component, name the time it broke, say what still works. B3's stale-tier copy follows it — 'we stopped at 14:02 UTC and we know about it' — rather than a spinner.
healthchecks.io as the external dead-man's switch: the standard cheap answer to 'who watches the watchdog', and the only observer nothing inside the system can silence.
